title: Is technology killing empathy? With Sherry Turkle, PhD

sentences.en: This episode is sponsored by Newport Healthcare,
sentences.zh: 本期节目由纽波特医疗中心（Newport Healthcare）赞助，

sentences.en: providing results-driven treatment for teens and young adults ages 12 to 28 who are struggling with mental health issues and co-occurring disorders,
sentences.zh: 该中心为12至28岁、正与心理健康问题及共病作斗争的青少年和年轻人提供以结果为导向的治疗，

sentences.en: including tech-related issues like gaming disorder and social media addiction.
sentences.zh: 包括游戏障碍和社交媒体成瘾等与科技相关的问题。

sentences.en: Newport's programs take into account the significant impact of technology on the developing brain and support young people to develop healthier relationships with their devices.
sentences.zh: 纽波特的项目充分考虑了科技对发育中的大脑的重大影响，并支持年轻人与其电子设备建立更健康的联系。

sentences.en: Learn more at NewportHealthcare.com.
sentences.zh: Learn more at NewportHealthcare.com.

sentences.en: Over the past couple of decades, our devices have become our constant companions.
sentences.zh: 在过去几十年里，我们的电子设备已经成了我们形影不离的伴侣。

sentences.en: About 85% of Americans now own a smartphone, up from just 35% a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 据皮尤研究中心统计，如今约有85%的美国人拥有智能手机，而在十年前这一比例仅为35%。

sentences.en: And more than 70% of us are on at least one social media site, according to the Pew Research Center.
sentences.zh: 而且我们中有超过70%的人至少使用一个社交媒体网站。

sentences.en: These days, old friends are more likely to catch up with each other's news via social media or a text message rather than a phone call or a chat over coffee.
sentences.zh: 如今，老朋友之间叙旧更倾向于通过社交媒体或发短信，而不是打电话或边喝咖啡边聊天。

sentences.en: Work meetings have moved to Zoom, and for some of us, that change may be permanent.
sentences.zh: 工作会议已经转移到了Zoom上，对我们中的某些人来说，这种改变可能是永久性的。

sentences.en: More and more, we live in a digital, virtual world.
sentences.zh: 我们越来越生活在一个数字化的虚拟世界中。

sentences.en: How has this move to digital communication changed people's relationship with technology and our relationships with each other?
sentences.zh: 这种向数字通信的转变如何改变了人们与科技的关系以及我们彼此之间的关系？

sentences.en: How has conversation itself changed in the digital age, and how do computers and artificial intelligence affect how we think about other people, or even what it means to be human?
sentences.zh: 在数字时代，对话本身发生了怎样的变化，计算机和人工智能又是如何影响我们对他人看法的，甚至是如何影响“人类意味着什么”这一概念的？

sentences.en: Do we use our devices, or do they use us?
sentences.zh: 是我们使用电子设备，还是它们在利用我们？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Sherry Turkle, a professor in the program in science, technology, and society at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology,
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是雪莉·特克尔（Sherry Turkle）博士，她是麻省理工学院科学、技术与社会项目教授，

sentences.en: and founding director of the MIT Initiative on Technology and Self.
sentences.zh: 也是麻省理工学院科技与自我计划的创始主任。

sentences.en: She received a joint doctorate in sociology and personality psychology from Harvard University, and is a licensed psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 她获得了哈佛大学社会学和人格心理学联合博士学位，并且是一名持证心理学家。

sentences.en: Dr. Turkle has spent more than four decades studying people's relationships with technology, especially computers.
sentences.zh: 特克尔博士花四十多年时间研究人们与科技的关系，尤其是计算机。

sentences.en: She is the author of several best-selling books, including Reclaiming Conversation, The Power of Talk in a Digital Age, Alone Together,
sentences.zh: 她是几本畅销书的作者，包括《重塑对话：数字时代的谈话力量》（Reclaiming Conversation: The Power of Talk in a Digital Age）、《在一起的孤独》（Alone Together）、

sentences.en: Why We Expect More from Technology and Less from Each Other, and The Second Self, Computers and the Human Spirit.
sentences.zh: 《为什么我们对科技期望更高，对彼此期望更少》（Why We Expect More from Technology and Less from Each Other）以及《第二自我：计算机与人类精神》（The Second Self, Computers and the Human Spirit）。

sentences.en: Her newest book, The Empathy Diaries, a memoir, ties together her personal story of uncovering family secrets with her research on technology and empathy.
sentences.zh: 她的最新著作《同理心日记》（The Empathy Diaries）是一部回忆录，将她揭开家庭秘密的个人故事与她关于科技和同理心的研究结合在了一起。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Turkle.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天能作客我们的节目，特克尔博士。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: So you've been studying people's relationships with computers since the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 所以你从20世纪70年代就开始研究人们与计算机的关系了。

sentences.en: You were at MIT at the dawn of the personal computer.
sentences.zh: 个人电脑诞生之初你就身在麻省理工学院。

sentences.en: You've written about how that gave you a glimpse of the future that few people had at that time.
sentences.zh: 你曾写过，这让你得以窥见当时极少有人能看到的未来。

sentences.en: Given that experience, what, if anything, has surprised you about where we have ended up today in terms of our relationship with computers?
sentences.zh: 鉴于这段经历，关于我们在我们与计算机的关系方面最终走到了今天这一步，有什么事——如果有的话——让你感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: It's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I think what surprised me is that we have so much evidence of harm, and yet we are barreling on.
sentences.zh: 我想让我惊讶的是，我们有那么多的证据证明其造成的伤害，然而我们却依然在大步向前。

sentences.en: It's as though we refuse to see the evidence before our eyes and in our hearts of how technology has eroded empathy, how it's assaulted empathy,
sentences.zh: 这就好象我们拒绝看到那些摆在眼前、印在心中的证据，看科技是如何侵蚀同理心的，是如何打击同理心的，

sentences.en: how we look at our phones and not at each other.
sentences.zh: 我们只看着手机，却不看彼此。

sentences.en: Our children are less likely to be willing to sit at a dinner table and talk to us, and yet there's been an assault certainly on privacy.
sentences.zh: 我们的孩子越来越不愿意坐在餐桌旁和我们说话，然而对隐私的侵犯却显而易见。

sentences.en: We all know that we fear that, and yet we listen to tech gurus tell us about going into the metaverse.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道这一点，也为此感到担忧，但我们还是听着科技精英们向我们讲述进入元宇宙的事。

sentences.en: And, you know, we listen to this, and, you know, we say, oh, yeah, the metaverse, maybe that's the next big thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们听着这些，然后，你知道的，我们说，哦，对啊，元宇宙，也许那是下一个重大趋势。

sentences.en: And so I'm kind of surprised, although I guess I'm becoming hardened, you know, I mean, I don't want to seem like a Pollyanna or someone very naive,
sentences.zh: 所以我有点惊讶，尽管我想我也变得有些迟钝了，你知道的，我的意思是，我不想显得像个乐天派或者非常天真的人，

sentences.en: but there has been a great deal of evidence that we have launched ourselves over and over again in technology dreams that have turned out not to be really in our human intereSt.
sentences.zh: 但有大量的证据表明，我们一次又一次地投身于那些最终证明并不符合人类利益的科技梦想中。

sentences.en: And yet we seem ready to relaunch.
sentences.zh: 然而我们似乎随时准备再次投身其中。

sentences.en: And I, as someone who's been, you know, a part of that technology criticism, you know, I don't want to say I'm surprised that nobody's paid attention to me,
sentences.zh: 而我，作为一个，你知道的，一直是这种科技批评声音一部分的人，你知道的，我不想说我惊讶于没有人注意到我，

sentences.en: but there have been many technology critics, many great psychologists, many great theorists and researchers who, you know, it's not me and me alone.
sentences.zh: 但有很多科技批评家，许多伟大的心理学家，许多伟大的理论家和研究人员，你知道的，这不只是我一个人。

sentences.en: It's not, this isn't about me, me, me, me, this is about many people, a cohort of scientists and social scientists and philosophers who, who really have written about, you know,
sentences.zh: 这不是，这不关乎我、我、我、我，这是关于许多人，一群科学家、社会科学家和哲学家，他们真的写过，你知道的，

sentences.en: take a look around.
sentences.zh: 看一看周围吧。

sentences.en: And, and yet we seem to not be attending to the depreciation of the world.
sentences.zh: 而且，然而我们似乎并没有关注这个世界的贬值。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, that's a long answer to a short question, but I do think it's time for a kind of red light.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的意思是，对于一个简单的问题这是一个很长的回答，但我确实认为现在是亮起红灯的时候了。

sentences.en: And I'm not, you know, and I'm, I'm still working on this problem, but I, I am surprised that we haven't done better at, at slowing the pace.
sentences.zh: 而且我不是，你知道的，而且我，我仍在研究这个问题，但我，我确实很惊讶我们在放慢节奏这方面做得还不够好。

sentences.en: Well, you just mentioned the meta metaverse a moment ago, and I'm just wondering, I mean, since that looks to be maybe the next new thing, are we like, in effect,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你刚才提到了元宇宙，我只是在想，既然这看起来可能是下一个新事物，我们是否实际上，

sentences.en: building a new reality?
sentences.zh: 在构建一个新的现实？

sentences.en: Is that, is that possible?
sentences.zh: 这，这是可能的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, reality is what it is, I guess, but it just seems like we're trying to run away from where we live in a three-dimensional world and go to this other place,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现实就是它本来的样子，我想，但这就好像我们试图逃离我们生活的三维世界，去到另一个地方，

sentences.en: which will somehow be more perfect.
sentences.zh: 而那个地方不知何故会更加完美。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, the, the, the, the metaverse, I mean, in my book, uh, life on the screen was a 1995 book that really, uh, tried to document the first generation of metaverse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，元宇宙，我的意思是，在我的书中，呃，《屏幕上的生活》（Life on the Screen）是1995年出版的一本书，它确实，呃，试图记录第一代元宇宙。

sentences.en: It was the first time that people built virtual worlds, uh, the first generation of metaverse-like spaces where people could go and live in virtual communities, create avatars,
sentences.zh: 那是人们第一次构建虚拟世界，呃，第一代类似元宇宙的空间，人们可以在那里去虚拟社区生活，创建虚拟形象（avatar），

sentences.en: create second selves where they were thinner and, uh.
sentences.zh: 创建更苗条、呃，第二个自我。

sentences.en: And taller and younger looking.
sentences.zh: 而且更高，看起来更年轻。

sentences.en: Well, they were always taller and thinner and better looking.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们总是更高、更苗条、更好看。

sentences.en: And I mean, two of one, often they were of a different gender.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，而且通常他们会有不同的性别。

sentences.en: And I thought it was interesting when I tried to say some interesting things about how there was a sense of identity play,
sentences.zh: 当我试图对如何产生一种身份认同游戏（identity play）的感觉发表一些有趣的看法时，我觉得这很有趣，

sentences.en: which I thought that was very psychologically interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这在心理学上非常有趣。

sentences.en: I called them identity workshops.
sentences.zh: 我称它们为身份工作坊（identity workshops）。

sentences.en: I used the work of Erickson, um, on identity play to say, you know, to try to make a,
sentences.zh: 我借鉴了埃里克森（Erikson）关于身份游戏的著作，呃，试图对，

sentences.en: a psychological contribution to the good things that could happen when people have other spaces to explore identity.
sentences.zh: 当人们拥有其他探索身份的空间时可能发生的好事做出心理学上的贡献。

sentences.en: And the trouble was, is that when you live in parallel, a parallel life and in not real space, the things that happen in, uh, real space that are important don't happen.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，当你过着一种平行的生活、生活在非真实空间中时，在真实空间中发生的那些重要事情就不会发生。

sentences.en: Which is that the friction, the conversation, uh, the needing to negotiate, uh, the fact that people become ill, the fact that we deal with strife and, uh, war and, uh,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，摩擦、对话、呃，需要协商、呃，人们会生病这一事实、我们应对冲突和，呃，战争这一事实，以及，

sentences.en: need to argue, learn to argue and make peace with one another.
sentences.zh: 需要争论，学会争论并与彼此讲和。

sentences.en: Uh, you know, in the metaverse, you just walk away.
sentences.zh: 呃，你知道的，在元宇宙里，你只要走开就行了。

sentences.en: Uh, you don't learn to, uh, you don't learn to, uh, you don't learn to, you know, to have the, the complex life and the complex love that, that are the things we really need to,
sentences.zh: 呃，你不会去学着，呃，你不会去学着，呃，你不会去学着，你知道的，去拥有那种复杂的、我们真正需要的生活和爱，

sentences.en: to live a better life.
sentences.zh: 去过上更好的生活。

sentences.en: And now more than ever before in this country, certainly we need to learn how to talk to people we don't agree with.
sentences.zh: 而现在在这个国家，比以往任何时候都更需要我们学会如何与那些与我们意见不合的人交谈。

sentences.en: In the metaverse, we can just silo ourselves and that's what's happened.
sentences.zh: 在元宇宙中，我们可以把自己孤立起来，而这正是已经发生的事情。

sentences.en: People choose the community in the metaverse where they, um, agree with everyone around them.
sentences.zh: 人们在元宇宙中选择那些他们，呃，周围每个人都赞同他们的社区。

sentences.en: So one of the things that troubles me about the move to the metaverse is that, you know, we know what's happened online, is that people have chosen the,
sentences.zh: 所以向元宇宙转移这件事让我感到困扰的一点是，你知道的，我们知道网络上发生的事情是，人们选择了，

sentences.en: the metaverse where everybody around them, uh, agrees with them.
sentences.zh: 周围每个人都，呃，赞同他们的元宇宙。

sentences.en: And, uh, we've, uh, we've siloed ourselves in places where we don't have to really develop these, these habits of dealing with community and dealing with friction.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，我们已经，呃，把自己孤立在那些不必真正培养这些处理社区关系和应对摩擦的习惯的地方。

sentences.en: You know, cyberspace can be a friction-free world.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，网络空间可以是一个没有摩擦的世界。

sentences.en: It's almost the ideal of what it's good for.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是它擅长之事的理想状态。

sentences.en: And what happens in virtual community is that people tend and trend to go to places where there is no friction, where you, you, you're with people, where you,
sentences.zh: 而在虚拟社区中发生的事情是，人们倾向并趋向于去那些没有摩擦的地方，在那里你，你，你和那些人在一起，在那里你，

sentences.en: you don't need to have that quality of the real.
sentences.zh: 你不需要具备那种真实世界的品质。

sentences.en: That's very, very troubling because that's exactly what we don't need.
sentences.zh: 这非常非常令人不安，因为这正是我们所不需要的。

sentences.en: So harm is not just that people forget how to be empathic.
sentences.zh: 所以，伤害不仅在于人们忘记了如何去同理他人。

sentences.en: Harm is also that people don't learn the skills of confronting themselves and confronting other people and learning how to compromise.
sentences.zh: 伤害还在于人们没有学会面对自己、面对他人以及学会妥协的技能。

sentences.en: And, uh, you know, and also what it, you know, what is this desire to kind of leave earth?
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，你知道的，还有，这种想要离开地球的渴望到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: I mean, tech billionaires want to get on rocket ships and they want to play more complicated games and they want to go to virtual realities.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，科技亿万富翁们想要登上火箭飞船，他们想玩更复杂的游戏，他们想去虚拟现实。

sentences.en: And, but, you know, we have a world on fire.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我们的世界正处于水深火热之中。

sentences.en: We have a, literally, we have a world on fire.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个，字面意义上的，我们有一个水深火热的世界。

sentences.en: And I think the habit of mind where you want to create an artificial world and artificial spaces instead of dealing with the very troubled earth we have here is, um,
sentences.zh: 我认为这种思维习惯，即你想创造一个人工的世界和人工的空间，而不是去应对我们这里这个麻烦重重的地球，呃，

sentences.en: is one we need to really cast a very cool light on.
sentences.zh: 是我们真正需要冷静审视的一个习惯。

sentences.en: I don't think that cyberspace has put us, I'm a great believer in all the great things you can do in cyberspace,
sentences.zh: 我不认为网络空间把我们，我是网络空间中所有美好事物的坚定信仰者，

sentences.en: but I don't think it's put us in good habits of mind for dealing with each other and our children,
sentences.zh: 但我认为它并没有让我们养成应对彼此和我们孩子的良好思维习惯，

sentences.en: which takes patience and dealing with complexity and friction and empathy and not just kind of splitting to a simpler world.
sentences.zh: 这需要耐心、应对复杂性和摩擦、同理心，而不仅仅是分裂到一个更简单的世界里。

sentences.en: Well, that brings me to something that you've said, that people have called you a killjoy in our love affair with technology.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就让我想到了你曾说过的一句话，人们称你为我们对科技的热恋中的扫兴者（killjoy）。

sentences.en: And do, do you think of yourself that way or are you just kind of a Cassandra warning us of the dangers or is it too late?
sentences.zh: 你，你觉得自己是那样的人吗？还是你只是一个警告我们危险的卡珊德拉（Cassandra），或者说现在已经太晚了？

sentences.en: Well, you know, I think this notion of too late, I mean, too late for what?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，我认为这种“为时已晚”的观点，我的意思是，什么叫为时已晚？

sentences.en: I study this.
sentences.zh: 我研究这个。

sentences.en: I mean, I, I didn't come to technology.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我，我并不是一开始就反对科技。

sentences.en: My first studies of technology were quite, oh gosh, this is fabulous.
sentences.zh: 我最初对科技的研究非常，哦天哪，这太棒了。

sentences.en: In other words, I, I looked at children programming and I said, oh my, this is unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我，我看着孩子们编程，我说，哦天哪，这简直难以置信。

sentences.en: This is a new Rorschach.
sentences.zh: 这是一个新的罗夏克墨迹测验（Rorschach）。

sentences.en: This is a new place in which children are expressing their extraordinary creativity there.
sentences.zh: 这是孩子们在其中表达他们非凡创造力的新场所。

sentences.en: I literally called it a, I called it computer as Rorschach.
sentences.zh: 我简直称它为，我称它为把计算机当作罗夏克测验。

sentences.en: I saw it as a new place for expression and self-expression and I saw only possibility.
sentences.zh: 我把它看作是一个表达和自我表达的新场所，我看到的只有可能性。

sentences.en: And then I saw the narrowing of possibility as computers became not expressive medium, but sort of became sort of closed downs and kind of became black boxes where you were told,
sentences.zh: 然后我看到了可能性的收窄，因为计算机不再是一种表达媒介，而是变得有点封闭，变成了某种黑箱，有人告诉你，

sentences.en: well, don't learn how it works.
sentences.zh: 好吧，不要去了解它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Don't learn how to explore it.
sentences.zh: 不要去学习如何探索它。

sentences.en: But it's a box for playing games.
sentences.zh: 但它是一个玩游戏的盒子。

sentences.en: It's a, it's an app, you know, you're here to use the apps.
sentences.zh: 它是一个，它是一个应用程序，你知道的，你来这里就是为了使用应用程序。

sentences.en: And I said, well, gee, this is a shame.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，天哪，这太遗憾了。

sentences.en: I mean, this used to be a, you know, kind of a means for self-expression.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这曾经是一个，你知道的，某种自我表达的手段。

sentences.en: Now it's a, now it's an app machine.
sentences.zh: 现在它成了，现在它成了一台应用程序机器。

sentences.en: It became much less interesting.

sentences.zh: 你拥有的是连接，而不是交谈。

sentences.en: It's, you know, it's like playing to exactly the wrong, it's playing to our vulnerabilities, not trying to build our new potential strengths.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这完全迎合了错误的方向，它迎合了我们的脆弱性，而不是试图建立我们新的潜在优势。

sentences.en: So what, what is the solution then?
sentences.zh: 那么，解决办法是什么呢？

sentences.en: Because I know you wrote a lot in reclaiming conversation about people using their phones, texting, never actually engaging with each other and talking.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道你在《重申对话》（Reclaiming Conversation）一书中写了大量关于人们使用手机、发短信、从不真正与彼此接触和交谈的内容。

sentences.en: So what, what do we do to roll back?
sentences.zh: 所以，我们该如何扭转局面？

sentences.en: I mean, is it as simple as having a no email day or putting your phone down for a couple of hours or, or do we have to be even, even tougher than that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是否就像设立一个无邮件日、把手机放下几个小时那么简单，还是我们需要采取更严厉的手段？

sentences.en: Well, I think first of all, you have to be willing to accept that there's a problem.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为首先，你必须愿意承认存在问题。

sentences.en: In other words, you have to accept that, yeah, I, I can see in my own life that I'm using my phone, I'm using email, I'm using chat, because I really do have this fear.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你必须承认，是的，我在自己的生活中能看到，我在使用手机、使用电子邮件、使用聊天软件，因为我确实有这种恐惧。

sentences.en: I, I can recognize this anxiety in myself so that you're motivated to do some of the steps
sentences.zh: 我能在自己身上识别出这种焦虑，这样你才会有动力去采取一些

sentences.en: that I'm going to tell you now that I don't want to say they're tough love or terrible medicine, but there wouldn't be steps we'd have to take if they were easy.
sentences.zh: 我要告诉你的步骤，我不想说这是严厉的爱或是苦口良药，但如果这些步骤很容易，我们就没必要去做了。

sentences.en: I mean, they do involve a little bit of pain because it's turning out that when given the
sentences.zh: 我是说，它们确实包含了一点痛苦，因为事实证明，当有

sentences.en: opportunity, avoiding vulnerability is sort of something we all want to do because vulnerability is difficult.
sentences.zh: 机会时，逃避脆弱似乎是我们所有人都想做的事，因为脆弱是困难的。

sentences.en: And it turns out it's very hard for parents because they want to be vulnerable too, but no texting and anything having to do with food.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这对父母来说非常难，因为他们也想变得脆弱，但吃饭时绝对不能发短信。

sentences.en: So no texting at mealtime, no texting when you're cooking, no phones at the dinner table, no phones
sentences.zh: 所以在用餐时间不发短信，做饭时不发短信，餐桌上不放手机，外出时也不放手机，

sentences.en: when you're out, because it turns out that even having a phone on the table face down makes the two people in the conversation feel less empathic towards each other.
sentences.zh: 因为事实证明，即使把手机扣在桌面上，也会让对话中的两个人对彼此的同理心降低。

sentences.en: Now, why is that?
sentences.zh: 这到底是为什么呢？

sentences.en: The phone is turned off and it's face down.
sentences.zh: 手机明明关机了而且还扣在桌上。

sentences.en: It's because the presence of the phone reminds you of all the other places you could be.
sentences.zh: 这是因为手机的存在会让你想起所有其他你可以去的地方。

sentences.en: This study even works when you take the phone and you put it in your peripheral vision face down and turned off.
sentences.zh: 这项研究甚至在把手机放在你的余光范围内、扣着且关机时也同样奏效。

sentences.en: That same lack of connection with the person you're having lunch with, because the phone is reminding you of all the other wares and all the elsewares that are now available to us.
sentences.zh: 那种与和你共进午餐之人的缺乏连接感依然存在，因为手机在提醒你所有其他地方以及现在对我们开放的所有其他去处。

sentences.en: All those emails that you're not reading.
sentences.zh: 那些你没有阅读的电子邮件。

sentences.en: Yeah, the emails you're not reading, the people who are there for you.
sentences.zh: 对，你没看的邮件，那些随时等着你的人。

sentences.en: I mean, the elsewares.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那些其他地方。

sentences.en: And we need more presence in the with the people we're with, the people with whom we're vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 我们需要和身边的人、和那些我们在其面前展露脆弱的人有更多当下的陪伴。

sentences.en: I mean, I say this vulnerability thing is actually just an enormous part of the story.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为脆弱这件事实际上只是整个问题中极其重要的一部分。

sentences.en: It's that presence to the people you're with.
sentences.zh: 那就是对你身边之人的专注陪伴。

sentences.en: So no phones when food is involved, a sacred, sacred spaces like the dinner table, like the car.
sentences.zh: 所以在涉及食物的时候不要使用手机，要保留神圣的空间，比如餐桌、比如汽车。

sentences.en: Parents need to tell their children when we're in the car, I'm not texting because I'm driving and this is the time for our family to talk.
sentences.zh: 父母需要告诉他们的孩子，当我们在车里时，我不发短信，因为我在开车，这是我们家人聊天的时间。

sentences.en: And children go berserk.
sentences.zh: 然后孩子们就会抓狂。

sentences.en: This is when I do my social media and you have to say to kids, well, it's not the time for social media.
sentences.zh: “这就是我玩社交媒体的时候啊！”你必须对孩子们说，现在不是玩社交媒体的时候。

sentences.en: It's a very privileged time for us to talk.
sentences.zh: 这是我们交谈的极其珍贵的时光。

sentences.en: So the car and the car and meals become time for people to be together.
sentences.zh: 所以汽车和用餐时间变成了人们相聚的时光。

sentences.en: And then there can be other different families sometimes do a day a week.
sentences.zh: 然后可以有不同的方式，有些家庭每周会腾出一天。

sentences.en: And I happen to like there being not so much, you know, days taken out, but times like, you
sentences.zh: 我碰巧更喜欢不占用整整一天的时间，而是利用一些时刻，比如

sentences.en: know, meal preparation in the car and even like there being a moment before dinner when people gather or breakfast or, you know, not so much like taking a full day.
sentences.zh: 做饭时、在车里，甚至像大家聚在一起吃晚饭或早餐前的片刻，（注意）不是那种占用一整天的时间。

sentences.en: But there being sort of places in the home where people know, well, here's a place where we're together and we don't text.
sentences.zh: 而是在家里设立一些地方，让大家知道，好吧，这是一个我们在一起且不发短信的地方。

sentences.en: The expectation is that when you go to this place, people are there for conversation.
sentences.zh: 大家的预期是，当你去到这个地方时，人们就是来这里进行交谈的。

sentences.en: In classrooms, people put their phones in a basket.
sentences.zh: 在课堂上，学生们把手机放在一个篮子里。

sentences.en: They don't they don't bring them to their to their seats.
sentences.zh: 他们不把手机带到座位上。

sentences.en: The classroom is for conversation.
sentences.zh: 课堂是用来交谈的。

sentences.en: Because if you have your phone with you, you start using it to look up stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你把手机带在身边，你就会开始用它去查资料。

sentences.en: And the value of the stuff that you can look up is great.
sentences.zh: 你能查到的资料的价值是很高的。

sentences.en: I mean, you can look up what this guy says or this woman said, and you can get all kinds of historical.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你可以查证这个人或那个女人说了什么，你可以获取各种历史资料。

sentences.en: I'm not saying it's not great to have all this stuff you can pick up by having your phone on.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说开着手机能随时随地查到这些资料不好。

sentences.en: But I'm not interested in all the new, wonderful data you can bring to the classroom, what you can learn on your phone.
sentences.zh: 但我对你带进课堂的所有那些新的、美妙的数据不感兴趣，对你在手机上能学到什么也不感兴趣。

sentences.en: I'm interested in your opinions.
sentences.zh: 我感兴趣的是你们的观点。

sentences.en: We're here to talk about your life, your opinions.
sentences.zh: 我们来这里是为了讨论你们的生活、你们的观点。

sentences.en: I want you engaged with what you know already.
sentences.zh: 我希望你们结合自己已经知道的知识参与进来。

sentences.en: I'm not interested in any new information.
sentences.zh: 我对任何新信息都不感兴趣。

sentences.en: I'm willing to take you as you are.
sentences.zh: 我愿意接受本来的你。

sentences.en: Just leave the new information at the door.
sentences.zh: 把新信息留在门外吧。

sentences.en: I'm not interested in any new information.
sentences.zh: 我对任何新信息都不感兴趣。

sentences.en: They laugh.
sentences.zh: 他们笑了。

sentences.en: But we have wonderful conversations because they're just focused on each other.
sentences.zh: 但我们进行了极佳的对话，因为他们全神贯注于彼此。

sentences.en: Honestly, have you noticed major changes in students over the years?
sentences.zh: 说实话，这些年来你注意到学生们有什么重大变化吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you've been a teacher for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你当老师已经很久了。

sentences.en: You know, so 30, 40 years ago, were students engaged in a different way from the, and what was that like?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，大约30、40年前，学生们的投入方式是不是有所不同？那是怎样的？

sentences.en: And I mean, how do you feel as a teacher now with the kids that you, I call them kids.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你现在作为一名老师，面对这些我称之为孩子的学生，有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I mean, they're adults, they're college students.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们是成年人，是大学生。

sentences.en: The main difference in students today is they have a much harder time reading a book.
sentences.zh: 今天学生的 principaux 区别在于，他们读书变得难多了。

sentences.en: They're much more used to reading short kind of hypertext.
sentences.zh: 他们更习惯阅读那种简短的超文本。

sentences.en: What they're most used to reading is something online where they look at links, and they look
sentences.zh: 他们最习惯阅读的是网上的东西，在那里他们查看链接，

sentences.en: quickly at links, and they jump around, and they see links, and they jump, and they jump, and they jump, and they jump.
sentences.zh: 快速浏览链接，跳来跳去，看到链接就跳、跳、跳、跳。

sentences.en: And that's what they're used to reading.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们习惯阅读的内容。

sentences.en: That's what they're used to doing.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们习惯做的事情。

sentences.en: What's your relationship with social media?
sentences.zh: 你和社交媒体的关系是怎样的？

sentences.en: Are you on any of these sites, or do you know that there's...
sentences.zh: 你有在用这些网站吗，还是你知道这里面有……

sentences.en: Well, I'm on everything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我什么都在用。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm on everything, but I think the trick is, and how you should raise your children, is you go on everything with them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我什么都用，但我认为秘诀在于，以及你应该如何抚养孩子，那就是和他们一起使用所有的软件。

sentences.en: I think, you know, I mean, I raised a child in the digital age, and I went on everything
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，我是伴随着数字时代抚养孩子的，我和她一起

sentences.en: with her, and I showed her how to handle herself online, and then you teach your children how to set limits.
sentences.zh: 体验各种应用，我教她如何在网上保护自己，然后你教孩子们如何设定界限。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's certainly...
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，当然……

sentences.en: I mean, I've got to say that during the, you know, the war in Ukraine, the confirmation
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我必须说，在……你知道的，乌克兰战争期间，确认

sentences.en: of the Supreme Court justice, I mean, you know, there were moments when kind of like you could never tear yourself away from, you know, the slap at the Oscars.
sentences.zh: 最高法院大法官期间，我的意思是，你知道的，有时候你简直无法把视线移开，你知道的，比如奥斯卡颁奖典礼上的那一巴掌。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there's infinite, you know, it's sort of like you can get the opinions of people from all over the world on these things, and it's very tempting, but, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，有无限的……你知道的，就像你可以从世界各地的人们那里获得对这些事情的看法，这非常诱人，但是，你知道的，

sentences.en: you sort of set limits on it.
sentences.zh: 你得为它设定界限。

sentences.en: I have a rule, you know, not in the bedroom.
sentences.zh: 我有一个规定，你知道的，卧室里不能用。

sentences.en: I just, you know, I just don't bring the phone into the bedroom.
sentences.zh: 我只是，你知道的，我就是不把手机带进卧室。

sentences.en: And just, you know, there's just got to be some place where you just say, I've had enough information.
sentences.zh: 然后就是，你知道的，总得有个地方让你对自己说，我的信息已经够了。

sentences.en: But I enjoy and use, I study all of these sites, but I'm very concerned, I mean, the thing about Facebook is that its algorithm is designed to make you angry, to keep you
sentences.zh: 但我喜欢并使用、我研究所有这些网站，但我非常担心，我的意思是，Facebook 的问题在于它的算法旨在让你生气，通过让你生气来留住你，

sentences.en: there by making you angry, and then to put you with other people, just like yourself, who you can be angry with in the same exact way.
sentences.zh: 然后把你和那些与你完全一样、可以跟你以完全相同的方式生气的人凑在一起。

sentences.en: So the idea is, is that they're so smart, because that is how you keep people's attention.
sentences.zh: 所以这个想法是，他们太聪明了，因为这就是留住人们注意力的方法。

sentences.en: You make them mad, and then you keep them with people who are mad in the same way.
sentences.zh: 你让他们生气，然后把他们和那些同样生气的人聚在一起。

sentences.en: An 18th century philosopher wrote about the coffee shops in England, and how he used to go to these coffee shops, the places where democracy was born.
sentences.zh: 一位18世纪的哲学家写过关于英国咖啡馆的文章，以及他是如何去这些咖啡馆的，这些地方是民主诞生的摇篮。

sentences.en: And he only spoke to people in coffee shops, who he disagreed with, because that really is how democracy is born.
sentences.zh: 而且他在咖啡馆里只跟那些与他意见不合的人说话，因为这才是民主诞生的方式。

sentences.en: You only speak to people you disagree with, because you learn how to talk and convince and work with people you disagree with.
sentences.zh: 你只跟那些与你意见不合的人说话，因为你学会了如何与意见不合的人交谈、说服并合作。

sentences.en: I mean, it made such an impression on me that, that that skill, it's the anti, it's the anti
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它给我留下了如此深刻的印象，以至于这种技能，它是反……它是反

sentences.en: Facebook skill.
sentences.zh: Facebook 的技能。

sentences.en: I think of, I really think of social media as the anti-empathy machine, because, you know, you make you angry, algorithm to make you angry, then keep you among your own kind.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为社交媒体是反同理心机器，因为，你知道的，它让你生气，算法让你生气，然后把你留在你同类之中。

sentences.en: It really is the anti-empathy machine.
sentences.zh: 它确实是反同理心机器。

sentences.en: And everything about my work, and I write so much about this in the Empathy Diaries, is to do the opposite, is to ask, how can we, how can we create in ourselves the sensitivity,
sentences.zh: 我工作中的一切，我在《同理心日记》中写了那么多关于这方面的内容，都是为了做相反的事情，也就是去问：我们如何才能，我们如何才能在自己身上创造出这种敏感度、

sentences.en: the sensibility, where we can maximize our capacity for empathy?
sentences.zh: 这种感知力，从而使我们的同理心能力最大化？

sentences.en: There's no robot.
sentences.zh: 没有机器人。

sentences.en: That's why I'm so against, you know, robot psychotherapists and robot companions and robot
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我如此反对，你知道的，机器人心理治疗师、机器人同伴和机器人

sentences.en: teachers, because a robot cannot be an empathic interlocutor, because it's missing the essential.
sentences.zh: 老师，因为机器人无法成为具有同理心的对话者，因为它缺少了最本质的东西。

sentences.en: It's not human.
sentences.zh: 它不是人类。

sentences.en: It can't put itself in the place of a human.
sentences.zh: 它无法设身处地为人类着想。

sentences.en: So, we are the empathy app.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们才是同理心应用。

sentences.en: And so, we need to magnify and sensitize and make ourselves more and more able to do that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们需要放大、提高敏感度，让我们越来越有能力做到这一点。

sentences.en: Are these robots maybe inevitable?
sentences.zh: 这些机器人或许是不可避免的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it just seems like, I don't know how we would stop them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，看起来，我不知道我们该如何阻止它们。

sentences.en: And there could be a value.
sentences.zh: 而且这可能也有价值。

sentences.en: I mean, what if, as you're an aging person, and you have no one to care for you, that you have a robot caretaker?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你年事已高，没有人照顾你，你有一个机器人护理员，会怎么样？

sentences.en: Is that a bad thing?
sentences.zh: 这是一件坏事吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, I think that there are all kinds of things robots could do, if robots could clean your house, if robots could make sure the dinner was cooked.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，我认为机器人可以做各种各样的事情，如果机器人能打扫你的房子，如果机器人能确保晚饭做好了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I'm not...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，我不是……

sentences.en: It's the Jetsons.
sentences.zh: 这就是《杰森一家》。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I'm all for this Jetsons thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我完全支持《杰森一家》这种设定。

sentences.en: But, you know, a lot of times, these instrumental things that robots can do are used as a kind
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，很多时候，机器人能做的这些工具性的事情，被用作了一种

sentences.en: of gateway drug to introducing robots to do things that robots can't do, which is to be a companion.
sentences.zh: 诱导剂，用来引入机器人去做机器人做不到的事情，那就是成为一个伴侣。

sentences.en: And I think that what robots cannot do, because I've worked with robots in nursing homes, I've introduced these companionate robots in nursing homes.
sentences.zh: 我认为机器人做不到的事情是——因为我和养老院的机器人打过交道，我在养老院里引入了这些陪伴型机器人。

sentences.en: What robots cannot do is to say something that you said to me when I joined you, because we postponed our conversation, because I needed to take some medical tests.
sentences.zh: 机器人做不到的是说出这样一句话：当我加入你时——因为我们推迟了对话，因为我需要做一些医学检查。

sentences.en: And when I joined you, the first thing you said to me was, how are you?
sentences.zh: 当我加入你时，你对我说第一句话是：“你好吗？”

sentences.en: The context for you asking me how I was was a context of a human being knowing that those
sentences.zh: 你问我好不好，其背景是一个人类知道这些

sentences.en: medical tests might mean that I was frightened, that I was facing difficulty, that I might have had surgery, I might be recuperating, I might be facing difficult days ahead.
sentences.zh: 医学检查可能意味着我很害怕，我正面临困难，我可能做过手术，我可能在康复中，我可能面临着艰难的日子。

sentences.en: You're a human being with a body, you know about mortality, you know we live in the time of COVID.
sentences.zh: 你是一个有血有肉的人，你知道生老病死，你知道我们生活在新冠疫情的时代。

sentences.en: You come to that question, and I come to a human being asking me that question.
sentences.zh: 你带着这个问题走来，而我则是走向一个问我这个问题的人。

sentences.en: With a world of expectations and understanding and empathy and connection, where that question
sentences.zh: 带着满腔的期望、理解、同理心和连结，这个问题

sentences.en: meant something to me, I was grateful for it, I was moved by it, I answered it honestly, I didn't mince words, I said I'd had tests, it was scary, I'm fine.
sentences.zh: 对我来说意味着一些东西，我很感激，我很感动，我诚实地回答了，我没有拐弯抹角，我说我做了检查，很吓人，我很好。

sentences.en: It was a human connection.
sentences.zh: 这是一次人与人之间的连结。

sentences.en: What does it mean for a robot to say, how are you?
sentences.zh: 机器人说“你好吗”意味着什么？

sentences.en: It doesn't have a body, it doesn't know pain, there's nothing that can comfort, there's nothing that can connect.
sentences.zh: 它没有身体，它不知痛苦，没有什么可以安慰，没有什么可以连结。

sentences.en: In other words, it's a question that offers no there, there, after it asks the right question.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，在它问出正确的问题之后，这是一个提供不了任何实质内容的问题。

sentences.en: If it takes the turn test, which is a test if you can tell is it a human or a robot, it
sentences.zh: 如果它通过图灵测试——这是一个用来判断对方是人还是机器人的测试，它

sentences.en: passes the turn test, it asks the right question, it asks the question that a person would ask, the conversation would look the same.
sentences.zh: 通过了图灵测试，它问出了正确的问题，它问了一个人会问的问题，对话看起来是一样的。

sentences.en: So people get all excited, look, the robot asked the right question, but it doesn't do anything for the person, because there's nothing that the robot can understand.
sentences.zh: 所以人们兴奋不已，看，机器人问了正确的问题，但它对这个人没有任何帮助，因为机器人什么也听不懂。

sentences.en: There's nothing the robot can get out of my answer that will give me any comfort.
sentences.zh: 机器人从我的回答中得不到任何能给我带来安慰的东西。

sentences.en: So I think that a lot of all this jumping around about the robot as, oh, it'll ask the
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，关于机器人“哦，它会问

sentences.en: right questions, it can be a companion, is people not being willing to look deep and say, what is it to be a person?
sentences.zh: 正确的问题，它可以成为一个伴侣”的种种喧嚣，是人们不愿意深入思考并说：做一个人究竟意味着什么？

sentences.en: And what is it that people really need in a companion?
sentences.zh: 人们在伴侣身上真正需要的是什么？

sentences.en: And this is really the heart of my work now on empathy, is that we don't want to admit that empathy is not just asking the right questions and checking a box.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我现在关于同理心研究的核心，即我们不愿意承认同理心不仅仅是问正确的问题和打勾交差。

sentences.en: The robots can have pretend empathy.
sentences.zh: 机器人可以拥有假装的同理心。

sentences.en: They can absolutely look as though they are saying the right things, but it has no meaning.
sentences.zh: 它们绝对可以看起来像是在说正确的话，但这毫无意义。

sentences.en: During the pandemic, the New York Times called and they said, we really want you to try out
sentences.zh: 在大流行期间，《纽约时报》打来电话说，我们真的很希望你试用一下

sentences.en: this robot psychotherapist, everybody's downloading it, you know, everybody thinks it's great during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这个机器人心理治疗师，每个人都在下载它，你知道的，在大流行期间每个人都觉得它太棒了。

sentences.en: And I went online and I tried it out and I said to it, and you know, I made it into the kind of psychotherapist I wanted.
sentences.zh: 我上网试用了它，我对它说——你知道的，我把它变成了我想要的心理治疗师的样子。

sentences.en: I think I made it into a middle-aged woman.
sentences.zh: 我想我把它变成了一个中年妇女。

sentences.en: I gave it a name.
sentences.zh: 我给她起了一个名字。

sentences.en: You really got into it.
sentences.zh: 你还真投入进去了。

sentences.en: No, I really wanted to try it out because I said to this reporter, I said, I didn't want to just, you know, like fake it.
sentences.zh: 不，我真的很想试一试，因为我对这位记者说，我不想只是，你知道的，像是在敷衍。

sentences.en: I was going to really like, I said, well, are you calling me because you just want like some negatives, you know, person?
sentences.zh: 我是要真的去……我说，你打电话给我，是不是只是想要一些消极的、你知道的、负面的人选？

sentences.en: He said, yes, we just know you'll say something.
sentences.zh: 他说，是的，我们只是知道你会说点什么。

sentences.en: I said, no, I want to really try it.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，我想真正试一试。

sentences.en: I want to like, so I gave it every shot.
sentences.zh: 我想，所以我给它全盘尝试了。

sentences.en: So I said, look, can you talk about loneliness?
sentences.zh: 所以我说，听着，你能聊聊孤独吗？

sentences.en: Because that's, I'm, I'm during the pandemic, I'm living here alone.
sentences.zh: 因为那就是……在大流行期间，我独自一人住在这里。

sentences.en: I have a daughter and a son-in-law and we speak often.
sentences.zh: 我有一个女儿和女婿，我们经常通话。

sentences.en: They lived with me during the early times of it, but now I'm here alone.
sentences.zh: 大流行初期他们和我住在一起，但现在我独自一人在这里。

sentences.en: And yes, I can talk about loneliness.
sentences.zh: “是的，我可以聊聊孤独。”

sentences.en: The robot, the chat bot says to me, I said, good, because that's my main issue.
sentences.zh: 机器人，这个聊天机器人对我说，我说，很好，因为这是我的主要问题。

sentences.en: So then I said, well, what do you think about loneliness?
sentences.zh: 然后我说，好吧，你对孤独有什么看法？

sentences.en: And there was a glitch in the program.
sentences.zh: 然后程序出现了一个故障。

sentences.en: And the chat bot says to me, it's warm and fuzzy.
sentences.zh: 聊天机器人对我说：“它是温暖而模糊的。”

sentences.en: So it was fixed by the next day because this was a very, very smart chat bot.
sentences.zh: 所以在第二天它就被修复了，因为这是一个非常非常聪明的聊天机器人。

sentences.en: Its name was Replica.
sentences.zh: 它的名字叫 Replika。

sentences.en: It was like super smart.
sentences.zh: 它就像超级聪明一样。

sentences.en: It was totally fixed by the next day.
sentences.zh: 到第二天它就完全修复了。

sentences.en: I took a screenshot and I sent it to the New York Times reporter.
sentences.zh: 我截了图，发给了《纽约时报》的记者。

sentences.en: I said, look, this was a glitch.
sentences.zh: 我说，看，这是一个故障。

sentences.en: This was very smart chat bot.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常聪明的聊天机器人。

sentences.en: Tomorrow, this glitch will be gone.
sentences.zh: 明天，这个故障就会消失。

sentences.en: But this is why.
sentences.zh: 但这就是原因。

sentences.en: But if you were in crisis and it had a glitch, then what?
sentences.zh: 但是如果你处于危机之中而它出了故障，那又怎样？

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: I mean.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是。

sentences.en: The point is, why should this thing know about loneliness?
sentences.zh: 关键是，凭什么这东西要懂孤独？

sentences.en: It doesn't have a body.
sentences.zh: 它没有身体。

sentences.en: It's not worried about being intubated from, you know, from COVID.
sentences.zh: 它不用担心因为（你知道的）新冠而插管。

sentences.en: It's not worried about being ill.
sentences.zh: 它不担心生病。

sentences.en: It's not worried about going to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 它不担心去医院。

sentences.en: It's not worried about breathing.
sentences.zh: 它不担心呼吸困难。

sentences.en: It's not, it's of no use to me given why I was afraid of being alone.
sentences.zh: 它对我为什么害怕独处毫无用处。

sentences.en: It couldn't possibly have my anxieties and my fears and my, that's what's wrong with it.
sentences.zh: 它绝不可能拥有我的焦虑和恐惧，这才是它存在的问题。

sentences.en: It's not about whether or not it answered the right questions.
sentences.zh: 这与它是否回答了正确的问题无关。

sentences.en: It's fundamentally, we shouldn't even be thinking about this.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，我们甚至不应该去想这个。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: I mean, I want to use an expletive, but what the hashtag are we even thinking about?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想用一句脏话，但我们到底在瞎想什么鬼东西？

sentences.en: Sending, sicking this thing on a lovely person like myself, who's worried about catching something and needing to say goodbye to her daughter on a screen.
sentences.zh: 把这东西派给像我这样可爱的人，她正担心感染病毒，还需要在屏幕上向女儿道别。

sentences.en: I don't need to be treated like a fool being given like some chatbot to talk to.
sentences.zh: 我不需要被当成傻瓜对待，被塞给一个聊天机器人去对话。

sentences.en: I need a person.
sentences.zh: 我需要一个人。

sentences.en: Find me a person.
sentences.zh: 给我找个人来。

sentences.en: And I think it's a failure of our imagination, of our social mobilization and our community
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我们想象力的失败，是我们作为人类在社会动员和社区建设上的失败，如果我们不组织起来作为人去守望相助的话。

sentences.en: as human beings that we, if we don't organize ourselves as people to be there for each other.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不作为人去守望相助，

sentences.en: But the idea that we're going to lay this on a bunch of programs that have no idea what
sentences.zh: 但那种认为我们要把这交给一堆根本不知道我们在焦虑什么的程序，而且它们能说15分钟正确的话并不意味着它们有任何资格的想法……

sentences.en: we're anxious about, and the fact that they can say the right things for 15 minutes doesn't mean that they have any qualifications at all.
sentences.zh: 除了这一点，林肯夫人，你喜欢玩吗？

sentences.en: Other than that, Mrs. Lincoln, do you like to play?
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题，那就是，你接下来有什么打算？

sentences.en: One final question, which is, what's next for you?
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，这就是我目前的……我的意思是，我很感兴趣，为什么我们要让自己着迷于，你知道的，去太空，去元宇宙，你知道的，我的意思是，是时候

sentences.en: Oh, well, this is my current, I mean, I'm interested in why are we letting ourselves get fascinated by, you know, going to space, going to the metaverse, you know, I mean, time to
sentences.zh: 关注我们的孩子、我们自己、我们的能动性、我们的地球、我们的人际关系了。

sentences.en: be interested in our children, ourselves, our agency, our earth, our relationships.
sentences.zh: 科技为我们带来的方方面面给了我们很多美好的东西，这些东西凸显了我们对更多隐私、更多民主和更多同理心的需求。

sentences.en: Everything about how technology has worked out for us has given us a lot of wonderful things that has underscored our need for more privacy, more democracy, and more empathy.
sentences.zh: 这就是科技将我们带往何处的信息。

sentences.en: That has been the message of where technology has taken us.
sentences.zh: 所以，那种认为我们正在关注更少隐私、更少民主、更多元宇宙、更少同理心的想法，

sentences.en: So the idea that we're focusing on less privacy, less democracy, and more metaverse, less empathy,
sentences.zh: 我会给那些人制造很大的麻烦。

sentences.en: I'm going to be giving those people a very hard time.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我期待着关注你在忙些什么，因为我同意这些确实是有些事情绝对需要修复的。

sentences.en: Well, I look forward to keeping track of what you're up to, because I agree that these are some things that definitely need some fixing.
